questions.question: DC-1 — Under macOS /bin/bash 3.2, `git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF' … EOF)"` breaks: an odd ' " ` or ( gives a syntax error, and a ) silently ends the message early. Craft never teaches this idiom; the harness defaults (Claude Code, copilot) do. How should craft respond?

options.label: Teach in core (Recommended)
options.description: Add one line to contracts/core.md, which every phase spawn gets in both agent and inline mode: commit with git commit -m "<msg>" (one double-quoted -m per paragraph), or -F <file> when the message holds " $ ` \ !. Never use the heredoc idiom. Also add a CORE_MARKERS pin and the docs. Costs about 240 bytes per spawn.

options.label: Document only
options.description: Only copilot README and gate.md gain the workaround. No contract change; roles keep the harness default, which fails or writes a wrong message on bash 3.2.

options.label: Teach in bundles
options.description: Put the same line in the producer/construction/refinement/harness-exec/delivery bundles. Review spawns skip it, but the rule is repeated 5 times, and the decisions phase, which commits ADRs and has no bundle, never gets it.

questions.question: DC-2 — SECURITY: copilot's plain-command gate accepts the idiom and treats its body as data. I reproduced the following myself: `git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'⏎x)"; git branch -D victim; echo "⏎EOF⏎)"` is ALLOWED by copilotGuard, and /bin/bash 3.2 then deleted branch `victim` in a throwaway repo. Plain `git branch -D victim` is DENIED. zsh keeps the branch. Not run live through copilot. What should the gate do?

options.label: Deny the idiom (Recommended)
options.description: Delete the idiom special case in git-plain-command-gate.js. The idiom then falls under the existing deny for `$` inside double quotes. Fails closed, removes code, and costs one re-issue in the taught form. Needs a refining ADR on ADR-595.

options.label: Keep, list as residual
options.description: Keep accepting the idiom and document the bash-3.2 early-close smuggle as an accepted residual. Smallest change; the bypass stays open.

options.label: Allow safe bodies only
options.description: Accept the idiom only when the body has no ' " ` ( ). This needs a character set pinned against bash 3.2's scanner, any gap fails open, and it denies most real bodies anyway.

PR #71 is merged into main as `e7f39cf`: https://github.com/scolladon/craft/pull/71. Craft now teaches a commit form that bash 3.2 parses, and copilot's guard denies the heredoc commit idiom. That guard denial also closes a way to slip a destructive git command past the guard.

**What bash 3.2 does with the idiom.** I reproduced this with macOS `/bin/bash` 3.2.57; there is no bash 5 on this machine.
- **Syntax error, no commit:** the body of `git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF' … EOF)"` holds an odd `'`, `"` or backtick, or an unbalanced `(`.
- **Wrong message, exit 0:** an unbalanced `)` ends the message early and runs the rest of the body as shell.
- **Guard bypass:** `git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'⏎x)"; git branch -D victim; echo "⏎EOF⏎)"` was allowed by copilot's guard, and bash 3.2 then deleted the `victim` branch in a throwaway repo. Plain `git branch -D victim` was denied. zsh treats the whole body as text.
- **Not tested live:** none of this was run through a real copilot session.

**Decisions:**
- **Commit form:** you chose to teach it in the core contract. The new `Commit form:` line in `contracts/core.md` says: use `git commit -m "<message>"`, one double-quoted `-m` per paragraph. When the message holds `" $ ` \ !`, use `git commit -F <file>` instead. Never use the heredoc idiom. This is ADR-605.
- **Copilot guard:** you chose to deny the idiom. Its special case is deleted, so the guard now refuses it as too complex to verify near git. This is ADR-606 and replaces that part of ADR-595.
- **Fallback:** `-F <file>` was taken as the design recommended (ADR-607).

**What changed in the review:** one real limit surfaced. On copilot, the `-F` message file can't be written by the file-creation tool outside the working tree. It has to be written by a separate shell command that doesn't mention git. A message that names git and holds `$` or a backtick can't be written that way at all, so it has to be reworded. The copilot README, the gate spec and ADR-607 now say this.

**Checks:**
- `bash scripts/ci.sh` and the PR's CI were green.
- Mutation testing on the changed guard code: 13 mutants, 11 killed. The 2 survivors are the ones the code already marked as equivalent before this change.
- The backlog entry is marked delivered.
- Metrics and memory are committed to main as `98771b5`. The push used the admin bypass, as expected.
